title: The Ring of Fire
logline: At a night procession, a fire performer whirls a torch and the crowd sees a ring of fire. Up close there is only one flame, a pair of hands, and years of practice.

object.note: Object 1 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The question of how much we 'know' through the senses moves from the tongue to the eye: at night, a single flame that a crowd sees as a ring.

thread_out.thread: From a procession's fire to a neighbourhood's paper lights: something built with great care, seen for a few nights, then taken apart.

lesson.in_simple_terms: When a torch is whirled fast in the dark, people see a ring of fire, but there is only one moving flame. The texts use this picture for how named things can seem whole, and describe the mind itself as a fast stream of moments that feels like one.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ගිනි පන්දමක් වේගයෙන් කරකවන විට ගිනි වළල්ලක් පෙනුණත් ඇත්තේ එක් ගිනි දැල්ලක් පමණක් වන්නාක් මෙන්, එකම සිතක් ලෙස දැනෙන්නේද ඉතා වේගයෙන් එකිනෙක ඉපිද නැතිවන සිත් පෙළකි.
lesson.the_teaching: One Abhidhamma text uses exactly this image: when a torch is whirled in the dark, onlookers see a ring of fire, yet only the torch is there, and the ring seems to exist because of its speed. It calls things held to exist only by such a notion concepts (paññatti), in contrast to the ultimate realities (paramattha). Another text describes the mind the same way: not one mind but a stream (citta-santati) of extremely brief moments, arising and ceasing so fast and without gaps that it seems like one. The ultimate realities themselves are described as momentary activities, not solid substances.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Wide shots give the crowd's view: unbroken rings and figures of fire over drums and darkness. Close and slowed-down shots show what is actually there: one flame on a stick, the performer's hands, wicks, fuel and burns, and years of practice. The viewer holds both views at once and may notice their own seeing doing the joining.

key_terms.en: conventional designation / concept; what is held to exist only by a notion

lesson.caution: This does not mean the performance or the performer is an illusion or that nothing is real; the flame, the heat and the skill are fully there, and only the 'ring' is added by speed and seeing.
lesson.builds_on: The taster showed knowing arriving through the senses; the ring of fire shows moments being joined into something that is not there, and turns the question inward, toward the stream of mind.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
